data.name: Parvej
data.gender_notes: Parvej is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Parvej is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Parivrajaka', which means a traveller or a mendicant. The name is also associated with Parvati, the Hindu goddess of love, fertility and marriage. Parvej symbolizes strength, courage, and protection. The name Parvej carries the meaning “Traveller, Protector, Moon” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit. Parents who choose Parvej usually hope their child will grow to embody traveller, protector, moon and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Parvej is a name with deep spiritual significance. It is believed to bring blessings of strength, courage, and protection. It is also associated with the journey of life and the inner strength required to overcome challenges and obstacles.
data.etymology: Parvej belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Traveller, Protector, Moon.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Parvej total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

historical_references.reference: Parvej was a renowned Hindu general who served under the Gupta Emperor Harshavardhana in the late 7th century. He is best known for leading the Gupta army to victory against the invading Tibetan forces at the Battle of Tarai.

Parvej is also mentioned in the Hindu epic Mahabharata, where he is described as a great warrior and charioteer in the army of the Pandavas. The exact time period of this reference is unclear, but it is believed to be before the 4th century BCE.
